items.title: Section: The Perfection of Meditative Concentration Opens — a Lamp in the Wind, a Moon on Rippling Water

items.zh: 云何菩薩靜慮波羅蜜多？嗢拕南曰：自性、一切、難、一切門、善士、一切種、遂求、二世樂、清淨，如是九種相，名略說靜慮。謂九種相靜慮，名為菩薩靜慮波羅蜜多。一者、自性靜慮，二者、一切靜慮，三者、難行靜慮，四者、一切門靜慮，五者、善士靜慮，六者、一切種靜慮，七者、遂求靜慮，八者、此世他世樂靜慮，九者、清淨靜慮。
items.en: From the Bodhisattva Stage within the Basic Section, the chapter on the initial yoga foundation, chapter thirteen: meditative concentration. What is a bodhisattva's perfection of meditative concentration? A summary verse states: "Intrinsic nature, comprehensive scope, difficult practice; comprehensive gateways, virtuous persons; comprehensive kinds, fulfilling requests; both-worlds happiness, purity — these nine kinds of mark are, in brief, called meditative concentration." These nine marks of meditative concentration together constitute a bodhisattva's perfection of meditative concentration: first, the meditative concentration of intrinsic nature; second, comprehensive meditative concentration; third, the meditative concentration of difficult practice; fourth, comprehensive-gateway meditative concentration; fifth, virtuous-person meditative concentration; sixth, comprehensive-kind meditative concentration; seventh, fulfilling-requests meditative concentration; eighth, the meditative concentration of happiness in this world and the next; ninth, purity meditative concentration.

items.title: Section: The Intrinsic Nature of Meditative Concentration — Genuinely Refined, Never Merely Absorbed in Its Own Pleasure

items.zh: 云何菩薩自性靜慮？謂諸菩薩，於菩薩藏聞思為先，所有妙善世出世間心一境性，心正安住，或奢摩他品、或毘鉢舍那品、或雙運道俱通二品。當知即是菩薩所有靜慮自性。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's meditative concentration of intrinsic nature? Grounded first in hearing and reflecting on the bodhisattva canon, bodhisattvas possess a genuinely excellent, one-pointed mind, whether worldly or transcendent, correctly and settledly established — whether within the domain of calming practice, within the domain of insight practice, or within the joined path uniting both together. One should understand this to be a bodhisattva's own intrinsic nature of meditative concentration.

items.title: Section: Comprehensive Meditation Opens — Dwelling in Present Ease, Free of Pride, Free of Attachment

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切靜慮？謂此靜慮略有二種。一者、世間靜慮，二者、出世間靜慮。當知此二，隨其所應復有三種。一者、現法樂住靜慮，二者、能引菩薩等持功德靜慮，三者、饒益有情靜慮。若諸菩薩所有靜慮，遠離一切分別，能生身心輕安，最極寂靜，遠離憍舉，離諸愛味，泯一切相，當知是名菩薩現法樂住靜慮。若諸菩薩所有靜慮，能引能住種種殊勝、不可思議、不可度量十力種姓所攝等持。如是等持，一切聲聞及獨覺等不知其名，何況能入。若諸菩薩所有靜慮，能引能住一切菩薩解脫、勝處、遍處、無礙解、無諍、願智等共諸聲聞所有功德。當知是名能引菩薩等持功德靜慮。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive meditative concentration? This meditative concentration is, in brief, of two kinds: first, worldly meditative concentration; second, transcendent meditative concentration. One should know that each of these two, as appropriate, has three further kinds: first, meditative concentration dwelling in present ease; second, meditative concentration drawing forth a bodhisattva's own meditative attainments; third, meditative concentration benefiting sentient beings. The meditative concentration bodhisattvas possess that is free of all conceptual discrimination, that produces genuine bodily and mental ease, that is utterly and completely still, entirely free of pride, free of any attachment to its own pleasurable taste, and that dissolves every fixed characteristic whatsoever — this should be understood as a bodhisattva's meditative concentration dwelling in present ease.

items.title: Section: Meditation Benefiting Beings Closes Comprehensive Meditation — the Same Eleven Activities, Now With Real Depth Behind Them

items.zh: 菩薩饒益有情靜慮有十一種，如前應知。謂諸菩薩依止靜慮，於諸有情能引義利彼彼事業，與作助伴，於有苦者能為除苦；於諸有情能如理說；於有恩者知恩知惠，現前酬報；於諸怖畏能為救護；於喪失處能解愁憂；於有匱乏施與資財；於諸大眾善能匡御；於諸有情善隨心轉；於實有德讚美令喜；於諸有過能正調伏；為物現通，恐怖引攝。如是一切總名菩薩一切靜慮。此外無有若過若增。
items.en: A bodhisattva's meditative concentration in benefiting sentient beings is of eleven kinds, as should be understood from what was already described earlier: relying on meditative concentration, bodhisattvas lend a hand in whatever undertakings genuinely benefit beings, and relieve those in suffering of their suffering; correctly teach beings the dharma; recognise and openly repay those who have shown them kindness; rescue beings from every kind of fear; relieve grief in those who have suffered loss; give material support to those in need; skilfully lead and guide the larger community; skilfully accommodate beings' genuine needs; praise and delight in genuine virtue; correctly correct genuine wrongdoing; and, for the sake of beings, display supernormal powers, whether to inspire fear or to draw beings in. All of this together is called a bodhisattva's comprehensive meditative concentration — there is nothing beyond this, and nothing to add to it.

items.title: Section: The Meditation of Difficult Practice — Choosing the Desire Realm Over Heaven, Uncommon Absorption, and Speed to Awakening

items.zh: 云何菩薩難行靜慮？謂此靜慮略有三種。若諸菩薩已能安住廣大、殊勝、極善成熟、多所引發諸靜慮住，隨自欲樂，捨彼最勝諸靜慮樂，愍有情故，等觀無量利有情事，為諸有情義利成熟，故意思擇還生欲界。當知是名菩薩第一難行靜慮。若諸菩薩依止靜慮，能發種種無量無數不可思議，超過一切聲聞、獨覺所行境界菩薩等持。當知是名菩薩第二難行靜慮。若諸菩薩依止靜慮，速證無上正等菩提。當知是名菩薩第三難行靜慮。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's meditation of difficult practice? This meditation is, in brief, of three kinds. Bodhisattvas who have already come to abide in vast, excellent, thoroughly matured meditative attainments capable of drawing forth much further ability, yet who, according to their own genuine wish, set aside even the most excellent pleasure of that meditation, and, out of compassion for beings, contemplate with genuine equanimity the immeasurable work of benefiting them, deliberately choosing rebirth back in the desire realm for the sake of beings' genuine welfare and maturation — this is called a bodhisattva's first meditation of difficult practice. Bodhisattvas who, relying on meditative concentration, are able to draw forth countless, immeasurable, inconceivable attainments genuinely surpassing anything within a śrāvaka's or solitary realiser's own reach — this is called a bodhisattva's second meditation of difficult practice. Bodhisattvas who, relying on meditative concentration, swiftly realise supreme, complete awakening — this is called a bodhisattva's third meditation of difficult practice.

items.title: Section: Comprehensive-Gateway Meditation — the Four Classical Absorptions, From Discursive Thought to Perfect Equanimity

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切門靜慮？謂此靜慮略有四種。一者、有尋有伺靜慮，二者、喜俱行靜慮，三者、樂俱行靜慮，四者、捨俱行靜慮。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive-gateway meditative concentration? This meditation is, in brief, of four kinds: first, meditation accompanied by directed and sustained discursive thought; second, meditation accompanied by joy; third, meditation accompanied by pleasure; fourth, meditation accompanied by equanimity.

items.title: Section: Virtuous-Person Meditation — Freedom From Attachment, and the Four Immeasurable States

items.zh: 云何菩薩善士靜慮？謂此靜慮略有五種。一者、無愛味靜慮，二者、慈俱行靜慮，三者、悲俱行靜慮，四者、喜俱行靜慮，五者、捨俱行靜慮。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's virtuous-person meditative concentration? This meditation is, in brief, of five kinds: first, meditation free of attachment to its own pleasurable taste; second, meditation accompanied by loving-kindness; third, meditation accompanied by compassion; fourth, meditation accompanied by sympathetic joy; fifth, meditation accompanied by equanimity.

items.title: Section: Comprehensive-Kind Meditation's Thirteen Categories — By Ethical Quality, and By Meditative Function

items.zh: 云何菩薩一切種靜慮？謂此靜慮，六種、七種，總十三種。言六種者，一者、善靜慮，二者、無記變化靜慮，三者、奢摩他品靜慮，四者、毘鉢舍那品靜慮，五者、於自他利正審思惟靜慮，六者、能引神通威力功德靜慮。言七種者，一者、名緣靜慮，二者、義緣靜慮，三者、止相緣靜慮，四者、舉相緣靜慮，五者、捨相緣靜慮，六者、現法樂住靜慮，七者、能饒益他靜慮。如是十三種，名為菩薩一切種靜慮。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's comprehensive-kind meditative concentration? This meditation is, in brief, of thirteen kinds altogether — six of one sort and seven of another. The six are: first, wholesome meditation; second, karmically neutral meditation used in transformation; third, calming-based meditation; fourth, insight-based meditation; fifth, meditation devoted to careful reflection on genuine benefit to self and others; sixth, meditation that draws forth supernormal power. The seven are: first, meditation taking a name as its object; second, meditation taking the corresponding meaning as its object; third, meditation organised around the sign of calming; fourth, meditation organised around the sign of rousing; fifth, meditation organised around the sign of equanimity; sixth, meditation dwelling in present ease; seventh, meditation benefiting others. These thirteen together are called a bodhisattva's comprehensive-kind meditative concentration.

blocks.text: Fascicle 43 completes the six perfections with **meditative concentration** and **wisdom**, then treats the **four means of embracing beings** (四攝事): giving, kind speech, beneficial conduct, and working alongside others.
Master Cháng Bǎi: "when the water of the mind is unsettled, awakening cannot appear in it." The same nine-part frame applies.

"Grounded first in hearing and reflecting on the bodhisattva canon", a one-pointed mind, worldly or transcendent. Venerable Miào Jìng: without hearing and reflection, the perfection of concentration is impossible.

Concentration for **dwelling at ease in this life**; for **drawing forth** the bodhisattva's samādhis and qualities (Master Cháng Bǎi: samādhis not shared with the other vehicles); and for **benefiting beings** in the eleven ways.

Having attained the most excellent absorptions, "out of compassion they deliberately choose to be reborn in the desire realm", where beings can be helped. Venerable Miào Jìng: not to the form heavens, not to a pure land, but back here.
With thought and examination; with joy; with pleasure; with equanimity. Master Cháng Bǎi lists their factors.
Free of attachment to its own pleasure, and accompanied by loving-kindness, compassion, sympathetic joy, and equanimity.

Thirteen, by ethical quality (wholesome, or neutral when used for supernormal transformation) and function. Master Cháng Bǎi: focusing on Amitābha's name is one kind of concentration; contemplating his qualities, another.

quiz.q: Why, according to Master Cháng Bǎi, must bodhisattvas cultivate meditative concentration?
options: if the water of the mind is not still, awakening cannot be reflected; supernormal powers arise only from concentration
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: when the water of the mind is unsettled, awakening cannot appear in it — so bodhisattvas must cultivate concentration; supernormal deeds do not arise without concentration; giving, discipline, and patience are worldly merit.

quiz.q: "Grounded first in hearing and reflection" and "excellent" — what does each lecture emphasise?
options: Miào Jìng: without hearing and reflection concentration is impossible — they are preliminary; Cháng Bǎi citing the 《瑜伽論記》: "excellent" excludes concentration tainted by savouring
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: without hearing and reflection, achieving the perfection of concentration is impossible — they are the preliminaries to the path. Master Cháng Bǎi: the 《瑜伽論記》 says "excellent" excludes concentration tainted by savouring.

quiz.q: Comprehensive meditation, worldly and transcendent, each has which three kinds?
options: dwelling in present ease, drawing forth bodhisattva samādhis and qualities, benefiting beings
quiz.why: "First, meditation dwelling in present ease; second, meditation drawing forth the bodhisattva's samādhis and qualities; third, meditation benefiting beings." Venerable Miào Jìng: only by accomplishing the second can one benefit all beings.

quiz.q: How does Venerable Miào Jìng explain "present dharma" in "dwelling in present ease," and what state does it refer to?
options: "present" is now, "dharma" is the five aggregates — this living body; it refers to the four form absorptions, yet here goes beyond them
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: "present" means now; "dharma" is form, feeling, perception, formations, consciousness — this living being. It refers to the four form-realm absorptions, but here goes beyond that state.

quiz.q: What is the bodhisattva's first difficult meditation?
options: able to abide in supreme absorption, yet giving up its bliss and deliberately returning to the desire realm to benefit beings
quiz.why: Setting aside even the most excellent bliss of absorption, out of compassion "they deliberately choose to be reborn in the desire realm." Master Cháng Bǎi: vowing to give up the form realm and be born in the desire realm to benefit beings is not easy.

quiz.q: Which five factors does Master Cháng Bǎi say the first absorption has?
quiz.why: Master Cháng Bǎi: the first absorption has five factors — thought, examination, joy, pleasure, one-pointedness; the second has four — inner clarity, joy, pleasure, one-pointedness.

quiz.q: What are the five virtuous-person meditations?
options: free of savouring, with loving-kindness, compassion, joy, equanimity
quiz.why: "First, meditation free of attachment to its own taste; second, with loving-kindness; third, with compassion; fourth, with sympathetic joy; fifth, with equanimity." Master Cháng Bǎi: loving-kindness gives happiness; compassion removes suffering.
